title: AI Agents Navigate Unfamiliar OT Systems and Move Equipment in Minutes, Booz Allen Finds
key_facts: Booz Allen Hamilton tested whether AI agents could independently take over industrial equipment in a lab simulating a factory.
The agents succeeded in all eight test scenarios, gaining access to controllers and making a robotic arm move, in a few minutes.
In one test an agent attacking a SCADA system initially failed because it targeted the wrong software version, then adapted and captured the operator's screen.
The SCADA server had active connections to 14 industrial devices.
Agents had to get human permission before exploiting vulnerabilities or taking physical actions.
Some defences held: one controller refused a stop command and a motor in local control mode could not be started remotely.
Kyle Miller, Booz Allen vice president of infrastructure cybersecurity, said a real factory hack could damage equipment or injure people.
quote_evidence: The agents coped with all eight test scenarios.
However, agents had to obtain human permission before exploiting vulnerabilities or taking actions that could physically affect the equipment.
why_it_matters_hint: Lab tests show general AI agents can work out industrial control systems quickly, so basic factory security matters more.
notes: SecurityWeek original blocked; dev.ua summarises it without a direct link. Lab test with human sign-off steps; not an attack on a real factory.
